StoredContentElement.title: Stored content element
StoredContentElement.description: A single node of the STORAGE model: what the admin edits, what validation and mutation operate on, and what the layout column holds. The same shape is accepted on input (the request `layout` and the attach `element`) and returned on output (the response `layout` and `orphaned`). Nodes nest recursively through `slots`. It carries the authoring wiring — data requirements, provided and accepted context, and binding attribution — none of which appears on a rendered response body; the rendered counterpart is `RenderedContentElement`. On input, only `id` and `component` are mandatory and the remaining members default to empty. On output `id`, `component` and `properties` are always present, and every other member is omitted entirely when empty rather than serialized as an empty container, so a bare element is a three-key object. Every empty map that IS serialized is emitted as `[]`, never as `{}`.

id.description: Element identifier. Any non-empty string is accepted except the reserved root literal `__page_context_root__` and strings PHP casts to integers (`0`, `12`, `-3`); apart from those two exclusions the id is stored verbatim, with no format, length or character-set requirement, so an author-supplied id such as `el-1` is as valid as a generated hex id. Element ids must be unique across every root of a layout. The mutation operations mint fresh ids server-side (for example `attach-element` re-mints every id in the spliced subtree); the minted ids are reported in the response `affectedElementIds`.

component.description: The registered element type this node is an instance of (the serialized `component` key). The set of valid values is registry-driven (core, plugins, and apps register types), so it is intentionally not enumerated here. Fetch the live list from `GET /api/_info/content-system-element-types.json` (the `name` of each entry).

properties.description: Authored property values keyed by property name, as declared by the element type. Every value is a JSON scalar, `null`, a list, or a nested map at every depth — a hydrated object can never sit here, because storage wraps each value in a variant type that admits nothing else. FQCN-typed (hydrated) properties are therefore not present; they are described by `dataRequirements` and `acceptsContext` and materialized only at render time. Defaults to an empty map when omitted on input; always present on output, where an empty map is serialized as `[]` (consistent with Shopware's JSON-map fields).

oneOf.description: The empty property map, serialized as `[]`.

dataRequirements.description: External data this element loads, keyed by the requirement key (which is also the property key the loaded value is written into). Omitted when the element has no data requirements.

slots.description: Child element subtrees keyed by slot name. Each slot holds an ordered list of child elements, making the layout a recursive tree. Omitted when the element has no slots.

providesContext.description: Context this element exposes to its descendants, keyed by context key. Omitted when the element provides no context.

acceptsContext.description: Context this element receives from its ancestors, keyed by context key. Omitted when the element consumes no context.

style.description: Universal presentation options keyed by option wire name (for example `col-span`, `align-self`). Each value is either a single scalar (a flat option) or an object keyed by breakpoint (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`) for a breakpoint-aware option, per the option's `breakpointAware` flag in the style-option introspection schema. Omitted when the element has no style.

attributedSpecifications.description: Binding specification attribution, keyed by property key: the source-qualified binding specification id (`source:id`, from the `bindingSpecifications` map on the element's type entry in `GET /api/_info/content-system-element-types.json`) that a `bind-element` call last wired that property from. Reconciled on every write — an entry survives only while the property's current wiring still matches what its attributed specification would produce, so a key hand-rewired away from its specification silently loses that entry, independent of every other key. Omitted when the element carries no attribution (never serialized as an empty container).

ContentElementDataRequirement.title: Content element data requirement
ContentElementDataRequirement.description: One external data source bound to an element. The hydrator fetches the value through the named `source` loader using `config`, then writes the result into the element property named by the requirement key.

key.description: The requirement key, which is also the element property the loaded value is written into.

source.description: The data loader source. The valid values are registry-driven; fetch the live list from `GET /api/_info/content-system-data-loaders.json` (the keys of `sources`).

config.description: Loader-specific configuration. The expected keys depend on `source`; the introspection endpoint reports each source's `configKeys` (per-key name, kind, type, and requiredness) and, per producible type, a `configTemplate` of inferable values. The keys a caller must still supply are the required `configKeys` names minus the keys already covered by `configTemplate`. An empty config is serialized as `[]` (consistent with Shopware's JSON-map fields).

oneOf.description: The empty config map, serialized as `[]`.

ContentElementContextProvider.title: Content element context provider
ContentElementContextProvider.description: Declares a context value an element exposes to its descendants and how that value is distributed to consumers. Distribution-specific members are present according to `distribution`.

type.description: Whether the provided context is a single value or a collection.

distribution.description: How the provider's value is split across its consumers. `broadcast` gives every consumer the same value; `indexed` is position-based; `keyed` matches a consumer property against the provider data keys; `sliced` chunks a collection; `iterator` distributes round-robin.

consumerAlias.description: Optional key under which the context is re-exposed to consumers. `null` keeps the provider's own context key.

keyProperty.description: Present only when `distribution` is `keyed`: the consumer property whose value selects the matching entry from the provider data.

sliceSize.description: Present only when `distribution` is `sliced`: the number of items handed to each consumer. A value below 1 is rejected on write; the lower bound is enforced, never clamped. Defaults to 10 when the key is absent.

ContentElementContextConsumer.title: Content element context consumer
ContentElementContextConsumer.description: Declares a context value an element receives from its ancestors. The received value is written into the element property named by the context key (or `propertyAlias` when set).

type.description: Whether a single value or a collection is consumed.

required.description: Whether the context must resolve. A required, unresolved context surfaces as an `unresolved_required` diagnostics violation.

redistribute.description: Present only when `true`: re-broadcasts the received context to this element's own descendants. Required for `consumerAlias` to take effect.

consumerAlias.description: Optional key under which the received context is re-exposed when `redistribute` is `true`.

propertyAlias.description: Optional element property name the received value is stored under, instead of the context key. Must not contain a dot.
